newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 16.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:

- Some producers of a common food additive are talking with the U.S. Justice Department to try to avoid potential criminal charges of price fixing in the wake of the charges against Archer Daniels Midland Co.
- General Motors Corp reported third quarter earnings of $1.27 billion or $1.5 a share against $642.4 million or $0.42 a share last year.
- U.S. Court of Appeals has temporarily suspended new rules governing competition in the local telephone business.
- U.S. freight railroad company Conrail Inc has agreed to merge with railroad company CSX Corp in a deal worth $8.4 billion.
- Texas Instruments Inc reported lower than expected third quarter earnings, while Sun Microsystems Inc reported a 46-percent earnings gain.
- Berkshire Hathaway Inc has agreed to acquire Flightsafety International Inc for about $1.5 billion in cash and stock.
- The Dow Jones industrial average ended 5.22 points down at 6,004.78, while prices of U.S. Treasury securities ended mixed.
- U.S. Labor Department will revise upward its tabulation of the number of layoffs in the mid 1990s to correct an error in its figures.
- Netscape Communications Corp will compete against IBM Corp's Lotus unit by launcing its Communicator desktop programme for the groupware market.
- PepsiCo Inc and Coca Cola reported their third quarter results on the same day for the first time in at least 20 years.
- Chase Manhattan Corp and Citicorp led a series of banks that released solid quarterly results.
- American Society of Magazine Editors issued a policy to defend editorial independence in the advent of corporate pressure.
- Brokerage firms Merrill Lynch & Co, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and Paine Webber Group reported higher quarterly results.
- A securities trader whose stock market bets caused college endowments to lose millions of dollars will plead guilty to fraud.
